habit_scope: Hold points for plumbing/electrical/HVAC rough after framing and windows, before insulation and drywall. 2-story light-wood. Not a how-to for the trades. CMHC Ch2+19+20. Notching limits are the carpenter hold.
also_known_as: MEP top-out / electric rough / HVAC rough
how_it_is_done: CMHC Ch2 sequence: after Doors and Windows comes Plumbing, Heating and Electrical Rough-In. Then Insulation, Air and Vapour Barriers. Exterior finishes can overlap insulation if protected from rain. About two weeks is the Canadian sample — not a headcount. No lag days invented. (Ch2 printed 21)

Plumbing (Ch19): begins after framing is complete. Roughing-in = vents, drains, and hot/cold piping that will be enclosed, plus the bathtub (tub before wall finish). Fixtures and accessories AFTER interior finish (that leftover is P16). 140 mm (6 in) stud partitions when the soil stack continues to another floor (Figs 151, 154). Horizontal soil stacks: headers between joists or a bulkhead (Fig 156) — do not sawzall the joists around them.

Electrical (Ch19): wiring usually after the house is enclosed. Roughing-in = wiring and boxes for switches, lights, outlets. Before inside finish and usually before insulation. Devices/plates after interior finish and painting (P16). 2-story: three-way switches at top and bottom of the stair. Smoke alarms hard-wired, in or near each bedroom on each storey including basements, on or near the ceiling — boxes in the rough; devices at trim. Airtight boxes in insulated exterior walls and ceilings. Switch height 1.4 m (4 ft 6 in) is CMHC Canadian — US device heights stay a Gap. Confirm AHJ.

HVAC (Ch20): qualified mechanical contractor. Map furnace, venting, supply/return trunks during framing to cut less later. Rough the ducts/piping. Combustion-air hole in foundation/rim/exterior wall as needed. Equipment set is P16. Keep construction drywall dust out of ductwork (Ch20 insight).

NOTCHING CMHC (carpenter hold, Ch19 Figs 148–150): never notch the underside of a joist. Upper-side notches near ends: within 1/2 joist depth of the bearing, depth ≤1/3 joist depth. Elsewhere on top: use a deeper joist so net depth ≥ required. Holes ≤1/4 joist depth, ≥50 mm (2 in) from either edge. I-joist flanges and truss chords/webs: do not notch or cut; manufacturer. Roof trusses: cannot be notched or drilled. Load-bearing studs notched/drilled >1/3 depth: reinforce with 38 mm (2 in nom) lumber nailed to the side, extending ≥600 mm (24 in) each side. Partition remaining ≥40 mm (1-9/16 in) need not be reinforced; bearing remaining ≥2/3 depth need not. Top plates in bearing walls: reinforce with 38 mm (2 in nom) if remaining solid wood <50 mm (2 in). Sheet metal may protect plumbing/electrical from gypsum fasteners. Holes closer than 30 mm (1-1/4 in) to a stud edge: metal protection plates (Fig 159). Penny not printed.

NOTCHING HUD / AF&PA US sawn VARIANT (already filed P07 — keep both, do not mix on one member): HUD RSDG §5.3.1 holes ≤1/3 member depth, along the center line. AF&PA Fig 28: no holes/notches in middle third; outer-third notch ≤1/6 depth; end notch ≤1/4; hole ≤1/3 depth and ≥2 in from edges. Confirm AHJ. One member, one table.

Wherever plumbing reduces insulation or cuts an air barrier: extra exterior insulation and keep the air barrier continuous (Ch19). Airtight electrical boxes in insulated exterior walls and ceilings (Ch19).

HUD RSDG OPENED: not a rough-in SOP (loads) — 1/3-hole is the US sawn variant above. Essential Guide OPENED: I-joist boring/notching is a framing book — already P07; drywall named as load/fire-stop, not a P12 hole chart. FM 5-426 OPENED: silent on MEP rough (names drywall hang in Ch 9 — that is P14).

tools_equipment: Trades' tools. Carpenter: reinforcing lumber; nail plates CLASS. Not a SKU list.
inspection_hold_points: Rough-in before insulation and before interior finish (Ch2/Ch19).
Building official inspects completed plumbing, electrical and mechanical systems (Ch2). Fig 2: Plumbing, Heating and Electrical Rough-In Inspection. No skip-inspection.
Never notch joist underside. Hole ≤1/4 depth, ≥2 in from edges. I-joist/truss: manufacturer / no cuts (Ch19).
material_classes: 38 mm (2 in nom) reinforcing lumber for notched studs/plates
typical_duration_sfr: CMHC Ch2: about two weeks — Canadian sample. No lag days invented.
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit hold. Not a competing method.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Insulating before rough inspection. Notching I-joist flanges. Skipping the bathtub until after drywall. Inventing IRC P-numbers.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They know rough-in. What they skip is the joist-underside never-notch and the inspection before insulation.
permit_gate: MEP on drawings; trade permits as AHJ requires (Ch2 names plumbing/heating/electrical/gas permits — Canadian list, confirm AHJ)
permit_gate_notes: CMHC Fig 2 permit list is Canadian. Confirm AHJ. No skip-inspection.
risk_if_swapped_late: Moving baths/stacks after framing is a joist/wall cut. Catch in framing.
plain_language_summary: After the roof and windows, the plumber, electrician, and heat man rough the pipes, wires, and ducts. Tub in now. Do not notch the bottom of a joist. Do not cut I-joist flanges. Inspector looks before insulation. Fixtures wait until after paint.
